items.title: Car-free school zones seek to protect kids from traffic dangers in Mississauga
items.summary: The city is seeking more Mississauga schools to take part in a Canada-wide effort aimed at protecting kids from the potential dangers of traffic. The national School Streets pilot project keeps cars away from elementary and middle schools at busy times of the day — early morning and mid-afternoon — when large numbers of students are entering or leaving the building. “By temporarily closing roads to vehicle traffic during drop-off or pickup times, the program reduces congestion and makes it easier for students to walk, bike or roll to (and from) school,” the City of Mississauga said late last week in reintroducing the program for the upcoming school year. The city has been inviting local schools to take part since it first joined the initiative in 2022. Mississauga public and Catholic elementary and middle schools that want to take part in the nationwide pilot program in spring 2027 have until Oct. 31 to sign up, the city said. Two schools took part in the pilot last year Sts. Peter and Paul Catholic Elementary School and Corliss Public School in Malton participated in School Streets during the last school year. During its nearly four-week-long participation in the national pilot this past spring, Sts. Peter and Paul, located near Rathburn Road East and Central Parkway East, cut off front-of-the-building access to cars at specific times of the day in a direct attempt to increase road safety in the immediate vicinity of the school.

items.title: Violent carjackings target numerous victims in Mississauga, across Greater Toronto Area
items.summary: Police say they’ve “disrupted a violent criminal network” that carried out nearly two dozen brazen carjackings and high-end vehicle thefts in Mississauga, Brampton and Toronto that terrorized and injured numerous victims. Peel Regional Police said Monday morning eight men and two youths face a combined 128 charges as a result of an eight-month investigation dubbed Project High Guard. The sweeping, multi-jurisdicitonal probe looked into 21 incidents of carjackings and other vehicle thefts that occurred across the Greater Toronto Area between June 2025 and April 2026. Investigators said at a news conference at Peel police headquarters in Mississauga that “knives and firearms were brandished and victims were physically assaulted” in a number of the carjackings. “In some cases, victims suffered severe injuries” and had to be hospitalized, police added. Detectives noted their “extensive” investigation also “led officers beyond the individuals carrying out the robberies and uncovered a coordinated criminal network allegedly responsible for planning, directing and profiting from the crimes. 4 million and seized four illegal firearms, along with ammunition and magazines. Speaking at police headquarters, Det. Sgt. ” The network allegedly had links to organized crime and those involved performed various roles within the operation, Peel police brass added.

items.title: Mississauga entrepreneur opens butter-focused retail shop and expands wholesale business
items.summary: A Mississauga specialty food retailer focused on flavoured butter has opened its first permanent store as its founder expands into wholesale distribution through partnerships with Ontario food businesses. Butter Bar Boutique, located at 1006 Lagoon St. in Mississauga’s Port Credit area, features the company’s gourmet flavoured butters alongside specialty foods, kitchen products, entertaining accessories and gifts, with an emphasis on locally made and Canadian products. Founded by entrepreneur Kate Engineer in 2023, Butter Bar has grown from a market-based operation into a retail business with production support from family-owned The Alliston Creamery. The company has also supplied its packaged butters to other retailers, including SanRemo Bakery and Downey’s Farm Market, with the products at those stores during the recent Thanksgiving weekend. The boutique’s opening and the wholesale expansion mark the next stage of a business that Engineer initially operated herself, handling production, packaging and sales before partnering with a creamery to increase output. Engineer developed Butter Bar after growing up around her family’s restaurant and working in retail marketing and communications. She later launched a fashion public relations agency and founded hospitality training company Servers Excellence before turning her attention to specialty food. For the first three years of Butter Bar’s operations, Engineer personally made, packaged and sold the company’s butter. She introduced the products at the Port Credit Farmers’ Market and expanded her reach through pop-up shops and the One Of A Kind Show. “I started Butter Bar out of a love for butter and cooking, and for the first three years, I did every part of it myself — from churning and flavouring to moulding, freezing, wrapping and selling every stick,” said Engineer. “It all began at the Port Credit Farmers’ Market and grew through pop-ups and the One Of A Kind Show. The support has been incredible.

items.title: Don't be so Salty: Mississauga to use Less Road Salt this Winter
items.summary: From cutting back on road salt to allowing fewer parked cars on the street during snow plowing, the City of Mississauga aims to keep snow clearing more efficient, effective and environmentally friendly. Mississauga City Council has approved changes to winter road maintenance. This winter, the City will begin a Low Road Salt Strategy and expand winter parking restrictions to include 15-hour parking areas. Together, these actions help improve safety for the public and City crews. Starting this winter, the City’s Low Road Salt Strategy will reduce winter salt use. The City already has a Salt Management Plan that includes pre-treating roads with brine, plowing more often, using advanced weather watch technology and using treated salt on colder days. The new Low Road Salt Strategy will build on the City’s Salt Management Plan and further reduce the City’s salt use by: Using more anti-icing brine—salt water—on 20 per cent more roads. This saves up to 650 tonnes of salt each winter. Plowing snow earlier on select major roads so less salt is needed. This saves up to 3,450 tonnes of salt each winter. Testing magnesium-treated road salt on select sidewalks and bus stops. This works well on surfaces for longer and may lessen the need to reapply salt.

items.title: Get ready to connect and grow! Mississauga is one of only three Canadian stops on the Startup Canada Tour
items.summary: Making its final stop in Mississauga, the Tour offers a unique opportunity to learn from expert speakers, investors, mentors and compete for cash prizes. Business and innovation | October 19, 2026 As one of only three Canadian stops on the 2026 Startup Canada Tour, Mississauga will welcome entrepreneurs, investors, mentors and business leaders from across the country to the Living Arts Centre on October 29. Building on the success of last year’s event, the Tour will connect attendees with industry experts, support organizations and practical resources to help start and grow businesses, while highlighting Mississauga’s key role as a hub for entrepreneurship and innovation. The Startup Canada Tour is presented by Pizza Hut, Scotiabank and UPS, with IDEA Mississauga and Visit Mississauga proudly supporting the Mississauga stop as local event partners. items.title: Peel police to announce results of probe into ‘violent’ network linked to Toronto-area carjackings
items.summary: Peel police also laid 128 charges after the probe into a suspected criminal network allegedly responsible for a series of luxury vehicles thefts across the GTA. Video released by Peel Regional Police showing a carjacking incident of a Rolls Royce Cullinan Luxury SUV. Peel police have arrested 10 men and laid more than 120 charges following an eight-month investigation into a number of “violent” carjackings and luxury vehicle thefts across the Toronto area. The investigation, dubbed “Project High Guard,” examined 21 incidents between June 2025 and April 2026 in which suspects allegedly used knives and firearms to threaten victims, some of whom were physically assaulted and suffered severe injuries, police announced on Monday. The investigation uncovered what police allege was a criminal network responsible for planning robberies, targeting vehicles, recruiting younger offenders and arranging the sale of stolen cars. At a news conference Monday morning at Peel police headquarters in Mississauga, Det. Sgt. Earl Scott of the service’s central robbery bureau said investigators were able to identify the multiple levels of the alleged organization. “We believe that they are the ones responsible for this network,” Scott said of the 10 people arrested. ” Investigators executed a series of co-ordinated search warrants on Sept. 3 across Peel Region, Halton Region and Toronto, resulting in the arrests of 10 men. Police would later lay 128 charges.

items.title: Mississauga Transit Riders to See Route Adjustments Oct. 26, Extended New Year's Eve Service Among Holiday Changes
items.summary: The City of Mississauga reports that MiWay will adjust service on select routes starting Oct. 26 to better align schedules with customer demand and improve reliability. According to the city, the transit agency will also run reduced weekday service on select dates during the holiday season to reflect lower ridership. The city says customers celebrating New Year's Eve will get extended late-night service on select MiWay routes operating past midnight. According to the city, riders should check MiWay's schedules page for updated route times and holiday service details. The city reports the next planned service change isn't scheduled until Jan. 4, 2027.

items.title: Three Mississauga Mayoral Candidates Make Their Case to Students as Parrish Skips UTM Forum
items.summary: The Varsity reports that three Mississauga mayoral candidates addressed students at a University of Toronto Mississauga Students' Union election forum on Oct. 14, ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election. According to the outlet, Ward 2 Councillor Alvin Tedjo, former mayor Bonnie Crombie, and Ward 7 Councillor Dipika Damerla each took questions separately for about 30 minutes at the event, held at the Blind Duck. The outlet reports incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish declined to attend, and organizers said they had not received a specific explanation beyond her earlier decision to take part in only three debates during the campaign. UTMSU President Adam El-Falou, who moderated the forum, said the union invited the four candidates based on polling and wanted to give students a chance to raise concerns about rising living costs, unreliable transit and limited job opportunities. According to The Varsity, Tedjo used the forum to propose five new Bus Rapid Transit routes along Erin Mills Parkway, Dundas Street West, Lakeshore Road, Derry Road and Dixie Road, saying work could begin in his first term with dedicated lanes and signals to speed up service.

items.title: Brampton Diners Won't Need the Drive to Mississauga Much Longer as Mughal Mahal Plans Expansion
items.summary: Insauga.com reports that Mughal Mahal, a Mississauga restaurant known for its Punjabi cuisine, is opening a second location in Brampton. According to the outlet, the restaurant announced the move on social media with the message "Same flavours. New location." The outlet reports no opening date has been set, though the restaurant says the new spot is coming soon. Insauga.com says the restaurant specializes in Amritsari kulcha, a buttery stuffed flatbread from the Punjabi city of Amritsar that is baked in a tandoor and traditionally served with chole, a spiced chickpea dish. According to the restaurant, the new Brampton location will carry the same menu as the original. The outlet notes Mughal Mahal has been serving Indian food since 1990, according to its website.
